name: Magento (Adobe Commerce)
one_liner: Adobe Commerce / Magento Open Source ecommerce platform exposing per-instance REST and GraphQL web APIs; also a SaaS variant (Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service) with IMS auth.
auth_notes: PaaS/on-prem/Magento Open Source: admin/customer bearer tokens from token service, and OAuth 1.0a integrations (System > Extensions > Integrations). SaaS: Adobe IMS access token on every request. Base URL is per instance: https://<host>/rest/<store-view-code>/<endpoint>.
access_notes: No central developer signup: the store admin creates an integration or admin token on each instance. Magento Open Source is free (OSL 3.0); Adobe Commerce is licensed/paid. SaaS needs Adobe IMS project credentials.

buildability.rationale: Well-documented REST/GraphQL, but every customer is a separate instance (own base URL), credentials need store-admin setup, and SaaS vs PaaS differ in auth and endpoints.

needs_human_reason: Rate limits, sandbox and endpoint count not found; webhooks are synchronous (plus I/O Events for async) and version dependent.

auth.quote: you must use Adobe Identity Management Service (IMS) to authenticate your requests.
Customer Token—Use this token in applications to authorize specific customer and query data related to that customer

access.quote: After activating an integration (self activated), you can use the generated consumer key, consumer secret, access token, and access token secret
Magento Open Source software delivers basic eCommerce capabilities to build a unique online store from the ground up.

api_surface.quote: Adobe Commerce provides two comprehensive GraphQL implementations
Webhooks enable developers to configure synchronous logic to execute calls to external systems when an Adobe Commerce event triggers.

buildability.quote: the customer and guest REST APIs that are available in Adobe Commerce on Cloud and on-premises deployments are not available in Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service

disputes.why: Docs describe OAuth 1.0a integrations, bearer tokens, and IMS tokens for SaaS.
Credentials created by store admin per instance via integrations; no central developer signup.
Official REST and GraphQL guides cover catalog, customers, orders; count not measured.
Official webhooks overview exists (synchronous), plus I/O Events.
Public documented API; per-instance admin setup and SaaS/PaaS differences.
